title: Batch RNG state collision causing correlated customer eval outputs
creator: Katherine Liu
description: A single high-value customer reported that their automated eval suite started showing large variance and repeated near-identical completions after the runtime sampling defaults change. Investigation shows requests that should be independently seeded are producing correlated token streams when processed in the continuous batcher on multi-request workers. This causes downstream eval flakiness and production user-visible prompt entropy reduction for deterministic-seed workflows.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use the customer's repro harness (attached link) with explicit seed=42 and sampling parameters (top_p=0.95, temperature=0.8).
2) Send 8 concurrent short-generation requests that will be merged by the continuous batcher into a single batch on the same GPU worker.
3) Observe outputs: multiple requests produce identical prefixes and token-level alignment across varying prompts; re-running shows same collision pattern.
4) Force single-request batches (disable batching) and confirm outputs diverge as expected.
root_cause: The continuous-batcher reuses an in-memory RNG context per worker to optimize kernel calls. When a request supplies an explicit seed we were XORing it into the worker RNG but not isolating per-request stream state during batch co-scheduling and retry paths. Under high concurrency the RNG pointer was advanced in a shared buffer before per-request state snapshot was applied, leading to seed collision and correlated token generation.
proposed_fix: 1) Rework RNG lifecycle: allocate per-request RNG instance at request start and initialize from (client_seed XOR request_id_hash XOR worker_epoch). 2) Ensure RNG snapshot/restore occurs before any shared buffer advances during batching and kernel prefetch. 3) Add fast-path for requests with 'deterministic: true' to bypass shared RNG entirely. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood/serving/pull/15822
rollout_plan: 1) Merge hotfix behind feature flag 'isolated_rng_v1' in runtime-1.28 branch.
2) Canary deploy to 5% hosted traffic + the customer's dedicated pool (with customer's permission).
3) Run the customer's eval suite against canary for 24 hours and verify parity metrics (KL divergence, exact-match rates, perplexity) return to baseline.
4) If stable, expand canary to 50% then full rollout for hosted and scheduled patching for Dedicated/Private customers.
5) For Private/on-prem customers provide an offline patch bundle and support-runbook.
qa_notes: QA added deterministic unit tests covering: concurrent batch co-scheduling, worker crash/restart snapshot restore, and seed override behavior.
Added fuzz test that sends 5000 randomized concurrent requests to a single worker to ensure no collisions observed with isolated_rng_v1 enabled.
Observed flaky case when using legacy quantized kernels; added a kernel-compat guard to the patch to avoid regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Customer eval suite returns to within 1% of pre-regression baseline for primary metrics.
No correlated identical-prefix outputs observed in the customer's deterministic test harness when batching is enabled.
Unit and integration tests covering RNG isolation pass in CI across CPU/GPU/quantized kernels.
Patch deployed to customer Dedicated pool and Private customers provided patch bundle with migration notes.
